title: Texture Atlases, SubTextures & Sprite Animation Architecture

For copy-ready programs use the guides and demos; for current callable signatures use the source-derived API. Performance figures here describe reported experiments, not guaranteed frame rates.

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/TEXTURE_ATLAS_AND_SPRITE_ANIMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/TEXTURE_ATLAS_AND_SPRITE_ANIMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.
2D character animations, scientific sprite charts, UI icons, and particle effects require efficient texture packing to avoid multiple individual texture binds in WebGPU.
Retiam provides a complete sprite management pipeline:

items: **[`TextureAtlas`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/loader/TextureAtlas.ts)**: Ingests TexturePacker JSON manifests (hash and array formats) and combines multiple sub-images into a single GPU texture sheet.

**[`SubTexture`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/loader/SubTexture.ts)**: Mathematical abstraction representing a rectangular region on a parent atlas with normalized UV coordinates, rotational transformations, and whitespace trimming metrics.

**[`AnimatedSprite`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/AnimatedSprite.ts)**: Frame-based animation entity that plays sprite sheet sequences at precise frame rates with zero per-frame buffer reallocation.

blocks.text: Given an atlas of total width $W$ and height $H$, a frame located at pixel coordinates $(x, y, w, h)$ maps to normalized WebGPU UV coordinates $[0, 1]^2$:

items: **Whitespace Trimming (`trimmed: true`)**: TexturePacker crops transparent margins to conserve atlas space. The `SubTexture` stores `spriteSourceSize` and `sourceSize` $(W_{\text{orig}}, H_{\text{orig}})$, centering the trimmed sprite accurately relative to its uncropped anchor point.
**Rotated Frames (`rotated: true`)**: Rotated sprites swap UV coordinates during quad vertex construction to restore upright orientation without runtime matrix overhead.

For elapsed playback time $\Delta t$, configured frame rate $F$ (frames per second), and total frame count $N$:
When a new frame is reached:

items: The active `SubTexture` reference is fetched from the atlas index.
The quad's UV vertex attributes are mutated in-place via zero-allocation buffer updates.
VRAM texture binding remains completely unchanged because all frames share the unified parent atlas texture.
